correctness.rationale: The exact displayed 12x25 matrix has rank 12 and GG^T=0 mod3. Independently generated all 3^12=531441 primal codewords via vectorized GF(3) multiplication and reproduced coefficients 1,2158,39522,202272,236692,49992,804 at weights 0,9,12,15,18,21,24. Independently enumerated every normalized nonzero dual dependence on supports of size <=4, finding exactly one projective weight-4 relation on zero-indexed (0,18,19,20) with coefficients (1,2,2,2), and no smaller relation. Source MacWilliams transform produces the displayed dual enumerator summing 3^13. The unique weight-4 support is monomial-automorphism invariant; this does not determine the full automorphism group.
residual_risks: A single database representative only, not all 26 extremal equivalence classes; the invariant four-set does not imply a full group classification.

value.rationale: For a classified extremal self-orthogonal ternary code, the dual minimum support size, low-weight multiplicity, complete spectrum, and unique four-column matroid circuit are natural code invariants used to distinguish classes and constrain automorphism searches. The intrinsic unique support stabilizes under every monomial automorphism, giving structural content beyond an arbitrary weight histogram. One exact representative can be useful independently of a full 26-class census; no broader classification is claimed.
residual_risks: It is one database representative selected by file order, which limits generality and motivates future comparison with the other 25 classes.

final_claim: For the second Araya–Harada extremal ternary [25,12,9] self-orthogonal generator matrix, C_perp has exactly two weight-4 words ± with unique support {1,19,20,21} and coefficients (1,2,2,2), and the stated complete C and C_perp weight enumerators; all monomial automorphisms stabilize the support.
limitations: Only the second listed representative; other 25 extremal classes unclassified by this result.
Enumerations are complete for the given 12-dimensional code; not numerical sampling.
